title: Police Response Time Analysis, 1975
description:
This is a study of the relationship between the amount of
 time taken by police to respond to calls for service and the outcomes
 of criminal and noncriminal incidents in Kansas City, Missouri.
 Outcomes were evaluated in terms of police effectiveness and citizen
 satisfaction. Response time data were generated by timing telephone
 and radio exchanges on police dispatch tapes. Police travel time was
 measured and recorded by highly trained civilian observers. To assess
 satisfaction with police service, personal and telephone interviews
 were conducted with victims and witnesses who had made the calls to
the police.
